cold.index.ms.small.how: `fathom index` into a deleted store; p95 of the samples. Re-blessed by `reco-xsog` (2026-11-15) at the quietest of three bless runs on the container class this file's `blessed_environment` describes — the same 8 cpus, the same 7 934 MiB — whose calibration bench reads ×0.939 of this file's reference, so every time in this row is that run's own number divided by 0.939 to keep it in reference-machine units (§11.8); the other two runs normalise to 1 325.8 and 1 383.7 ms, and the quietest of the three is also their median. The move since `reco-15wk`'s bless is one defect, measured rather than assumed. The register row named the analyzer lane (`analyses` 828 ms) and two candidate beads and admitted nobody had measured either: declining the complexity pass outright (`extract.complexity.max_run_ms = 0`, the shipped spelling of “decline everything”) takes the phase to 212 ms — `reco-3h82`'s 209 ms — so the fill of `reco-l9bz.4` is the whole of the move and the risk vector of `reco-ydek.5` is none of it. Inside that pass, 313 of the 699 file sides it counted (45 %) were a content version the same run had already counted for the same path, so the run now remembers what it counted, per path, keyed by the blob each figure was counted from (`run_reused`, in `fathom index --json`): 619 → 372 ms for the pass, 826 → 567 ms for the phase. The counting itself is untouched — a repository whose files are each edited once pays every parse it always paid — and the budget is untouched too: **the 1 500 ms was never raised**, the row came off because the measurement came inside it, which is the only way a row on that register may come off. This box now reads the cold index at 1 253.8–1 376.8 ms p95 across the bless and gate runs taken at this tree (FLEET, `tests/test_perf_budget_contract.py`), about 10 % under the budget, and `phases_ms` says where the rest of the run is: `graph` ~590 ms, `analyses` ~567 ms, `episodes` ~39 ms, `spine` ~33 ms. The floor stays the 250 ms `reco-3h82` blessed against the fleet and is not re-argued here; it is wider than the ±15 % this row is meant to resolve, so the row stays on the list of ids the ratchet cannot resolve and the 1 500 ms budget is its guard. The `ubuntu-latest` leg is still not asserted against this bless: it was never measured at a tree that carries the analyzer-lane move, and FLEET says so.

rss.tui.mib.small.how: VmHWM of the TUI child, sampled after every keystroke, worst probe. Re-blessed by `reco-15wk` (2026-11-15) at the median of the three probes one gate run takes (33.4-33.62 MiB), on the container class `blessed_environment` describes; the centre is what the ratchet compares, because a worst-of-N peak cannot resolve ±15 % (`reco-dkr`). The floor is `reco-0zot`'s 4 MiB and it stands: at the TUI's peak the child's own dirty memory — `RssAnon` — is 15.0-15.2 MiB of this 33-34 MiB, and the rest is `RssFile`: how much of the 36 MB release binary the kernel had paged in, which is code layout and demand paging, not the program's memory. Rebuilding one tree with `-C codegen-units=1` moves this row to 30.3 MiB with `RssAnon` unmoved at 15.0 MiB — a 9 % swing out of a compiler flag, on a row whose whole ratchet is ±15 % — and a container and a runner read 2.4-3.5 MiB apart on the same tree. A floor that wide is a claim about the instrument, and `RssAnon` plus `codegen-units` are the two measurements that trace it; what the row can still red on is a move past 4 MiB, and the 120 MiB budget guards the rest.

note: Rewritten only by `make bench-bless`. Every value is a measurement, in reference-machine units (runner factor 1.0); a time budget gets the factor as headroom at gate time and an RSS budget never does (ADR-004 §11.8). Each value carries the noise it was blessed with: `center` is the statistic the ±15 % ratchet compares (the middle of the bless run's samples, because a worst-of-five cannot resolve a 15 % change on a 15 ms verb), `scale` and `spread` what that run said about its own scatter and `noise` the floor it was judged against — so a later run can say which ids it can resolve and which it cannot (ADR-004 §11.10, `reco-dkr`).
